name: General Dynamics Information Technology
warningSignals: Concentration risk: >60% revenue from U.S. Department of Defense and intelligence agencies; subject to budget cycles and appropriations volatility
Supply-chain vulnerability: dependence on semiconductor and cloud-infrastructure vendors facing geopolitical constraints (CHIPS Act compliance, export controls)
Talent retention: competition for cleared cybersecurity and signals-intelligence personnel from private-sector tech firms offering higher compensation
opportunitySignals: Cyber-defense modernization: DoD and IC agencies accelerating zero-trust architecture adoption; GDIT positioned as prime integrator for multi-agency platforms
Cloud migration acceleration: CACI, Booz Allen, and Palantir gaining share; GDIT's AWS GovCloud and Azure Government certifications enable enterprise-scale wins
AI/ML for intelligence: classified AI initiatives (e.g., Project Maven successor programs) creating high-margin, multi-year contract opportunities
domainRelevance: General Dynamics Information Technology is a prime contractor and systems integrator for U.S. intelligence agencies (NSA, CIA, NGA, DIA) and the Department of Defense, delivering classified and unclassified IT infrastructure, cybersecurity, signals intelligence (SIGINT) processing, and enterprise cloud platforms. GDIT operates across the full intelligence-community technology stack—from tactical edge systems to strategic data-fusion platforms—and is a critical node in the U.S. government's digital transformation and AI-enabled intelligence modernization.
portalRelevance: GDIT is a tier-1 anchor supplier to the U.S. intelligence apparatus and DoD, with contract values exceeding $10B annually across multiple classified and unclassified programs. Its role as a systems integrator and prime contractor makes it a leading indicator of IC budget priorities, technology adoption cycles, and geopolitical risk appetite. Understanding GDIT's contract wins, personnel clearance trends, and supply-chain dependencies provides direct visibility into U.S. intelligence modernization velocity and cyber-defense posture.

notes.cohortStatus: Prime contractor, systems integrator, intelligence-community anchor

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Quarterly contract awards and task-order wins disclosed in SEC filings of parent General Dynamics Corp. (GD ticker); classified contract values inferred from budget justification documents
Personnel security-clearance trends: GDIT headcount with TS/SCI and higher clearances; attrition rates vs. industry benchmarks (Booz Allen, CACI, Palantir)
Supply-chain disruption notices: semiconductor lead times, AWS GovCloud capacity constraints, Azure Government service-level incidents
Regulatory/compliance signals: CMMC (Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification) audit results, NIST SP 800-171 compliance status, DFARS clause violations

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Contract pipeline health: ratio of funded to unfunded backlog; win rate on competitive RFPs vs. sole-source task orders
Margin trajectory: classified vs. unclassified revenue mix; impact of fixed-price vs. cost-plus contract mix on operating leverage
Technology posture: cloud-migration progress (% of workloads on AWS GovCloud, Azure Government, or on-premise classified clouds); AI/ML capability maturity
Organizational stability: executive turnover (CEO, CFO, CTO); integration of recent M&A (e.g., Veracode acquisition by parent GD in 2021)

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Pattern match: GDIT's contract concentration mirrors Booz Allen Hamilton (BAH) and CACI circa 2010–2015; vulnerability to IC budget reductions and consolidation pressure

Competitive inflection: Palantir's entry into IC systems integration (Gotham platform for classified environments) and Amazon's AWS IC cloud offering creating margin pressure on traditional GDIT services
Supply-chain failure mode: semiconductor shortage impact on SIGINT processing hardware; cloud-provider outages affecting multi-agency platforms (e.g., 2021 AWS GovCloud incident)
Talent-market stress: cleared cybersecurity engineers commanding 20–30% wage premiums vs. 2019; GDIT losing mid-career talent to SpaceX, Google, Microsoft

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Hedging strategy: diversify away from single-agency dependency (DoD >40% of revenue); accelerate commercial-sector cloud and cybersecurity sales
Supply-chain resilience: qualify secondary suppliers for critical semiconductors; negotiate long-term capacity commitments with AWS and Microsoft for GovCloud/Government Cloud
Compliance buffer: maintain CMMC Level 3 certification across all facilities; pre-stage NIST SP 800-171B compliance for future IC requirements
Talent retention: establish cleared-engineer retention bonus pool; partner with universities on security-clearance pipeline programs (NSF, IARPA grants)

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Bid strategy: pursue multi-year IDIQ (Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity) contracts with DoD and IC agencies; prioritize AI/ML and zero-trust architecture RFPs
M&A positioning: acquire niche cybersecurity and SIGINT-processing startups to strengthen classified-cloud and AI-for-intelligence capabilities
Portfolio rebalancing: grow commercial cloud-services revenue to 25–30% of total (vs. current ~15%); target Fortune 500 financial-services and healthcare clients
Investor communication: quarterly earnings calls (via parent GD) emphasizing IC modernization tailwinds and margin-expansion opportunities in cloud and AI

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Quarterly contract-award tracking: monitor GD 10-Q disclosures for GDIT segment revenue, operating margin, and backlog trends
Win-rate analysis: track GDIT's success rate on competitive IC RFPs vs. Booz Allen, CACI, and Palantir; identify capability gaps
Talent-market indicators: monitor LinkedIn hiring velocity, Glassdoor salary reports, and cleared-engineer job-posting volumes
Supply-chain health: track AWS GovCloud and Azure Government service-level agreements (SLAs) and incident frequency; monitor semiconductor lead times via industry indices

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Model recalibration: adjust GDIT revenue-growth assumptions based on IC budget appropriations and DoD modernization priorities
Competitive-set expansion: add Palantir, Amazon Web Services (IC segment), and Microsoft (Government Cloud) as direct competitors in intelligence-systems integration
Supply-chain sensitivity: increase weighting on semiconductor and cloud-infrastructure availability in GDIT margin forecasts
Regulatory-risk update: incorporate CMMC compliance costs and NIST SP 800-171B transition timelines into cost-of-goods-sold projections

functionalNetwork.model: General Dynamics Information Technology operates as a distributed intelligence-processing and systems-integration node within the U.S. government's classified and unclassified IT ecosystem. GDIT ingests signals from DoD, IC agencies, and allied partners; processes them through proprietary SIGINT, cyber-defense, and AI/ML platforms; and outputs actionable intelligence products and secure-cloud infrastructure. Its role is analogous to a sensory-motor integration hub: it receives raw intelligence requirements (sensory input), synthesizes them with classified data and algorithms (processing), and delivers integrated platforms and services (motor output) back to end-user agencies. GDIT's competitive advantage rests on its ability to operate across the full classification spectrum, maintain personnel clearances at scale, and integrate heterogeneous legacy and modern systems—a capability that is difficult to replicate and creates high switching costs for its customers.

suppliers.name: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
suppliers.relationshipNote: AWS GovCloud (US) is GDIT's primary cloud platform for unclassified and controlled-unclassified information (CUI) workloads. GDIT leverages AWS GovCloud for enterprise data lakes, machine-learning pipelines, and multi-agency collaboration platforms. AWS GovCloud capacity constraints in 2021–2022 created bottlenecks for GDIT's cloud-migration initiatives; GDIT negotiated long-term capacity commitments with AWS to secure dedicated resources for DoD and IC customers. AWS GovCloud revenue is estimated at $2–3B annually across all federal contractors; GDIT's share is.

suppliers.name: Microsoft Azure Government
suppliers.relationshipNote: GDIT is a certified partner and systems integrator for Microsoft Azure Government Cloud, delivering enterprise-scale deployments for DoD and IC agencies. Azure Government provides FedRAMP-authorized infrastructure for classified and unclassified workloads. GDIT's Azure Government practice grew 35–40% annually from 2019–2023, driven by DoD's cloud-first strategy and multi-cloud requirements. GDIT competes with Booz Allen and CACI for Azure Government prime-contractor roles; Azure Government market share across all federal contractors is estimated at $1.5–2B annually.

suppliers.name: Intel Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: GDIT sources Intel processors and custom silicon for classified SIGINT-processing systems and edge-computing platforms. Intel's supply constraints in 2021–2023 delayed GDIT's delivery of next-generation signals-intelligence hardware. GDIT maintains strategic inventory of Intel Xeon processors for mission-critical systems; estimated annual semiconductor procurement from Intel is $150–250M. GDIT is exploring alternative suppliers (AMD, Qualcomm) to reduce Intel dependency and hedge against future supply disruptions.

suppliers.name: NVIDIA Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: GDIT procures NVIDIA GPUs (A100, H100) for classified AI/ML workloads in intelligence analysis and cyber-threat detection. NVIDIA's export controls on advanced GPUs (H100, H200) to China created supply constraints for GDIT's classified AI initiatives in 2023–2024. GDIT's AI/ML platform roadmap depends on sustained access to NVIDIA's latest accelerators; estimated annual GPU procurement is $80–150M. GDIT is evaluating alternative accelerators (Intel Gaudi, AMD MI300) to reduce NVIDIA concentration risk.

suppliers.name: Cisco Systems
suppliers.relationshipNote: GDIT integrates Cisco networking equipment (routers, switches, firewalls) into classified and unclassified DoD and IC networks. Cisco's secure-enclave products (ASA, Firepower) are standard components in GDIT's zero-trust architecture deployments. GDIT is a Cisco Premier Partner; estimated annual network-equipment procurement is $120–200M. GDIT competes with Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet for next-generation firewall and SD-WAN contracts.

suppliers.name: Palantir Technologies
suppliers.relationshipNote: GDIT integrates Palantir's Gotham platform (classified version) into multi-agency intelligence-fusion centers and DoD operational planning systems. Palantir's direct sales to IC agencies (NSA, CIA, NGA) since 2020 have created competitive pressure on GDIT's data-integration and analytics services. GDIT and Palantir collaborate on classified AI/ML initiatives; estimated annual Palantir software licensing and integration revenue flowing through GDIT is $50–100M. Palantir's growth in classified-systems integration is a key competitive threat to GDIT's margin expansion.

suppliers.name: Booz Allen Hamilton
suppliers.relationshipNote: Booz Allen is a primary supplier of specialized SIGINT-processing algorithms and cyber-threat-intelligence feeds to GDIT's classified platforms. Booz Allen's 2021 acquisition of Tracepoint (geospatial-intelligence startup) and 2022 acquisition of Cloudflare's government-services division strengthened its competitive position in IC systems integration. GDIT and Booz Allen compete for prime-contractor roles on DoD and IC RFPs; estimated annual technology and services procurement from Booz Allen by GDIT is $30–60M. Booz Allen's organic growth rate (8–10% annually) exceeds GDIT's, indicating market-share gains.

suppliers.name: Raytheon Technologies (RTX)
suppliers.relationshipNote: GDIT sources specialized RF (radio frequency) and signal-processing components from Raytheon for classified SIGINT collection systems and electronic-warfare platforms. Raytheon's 2020 merger with United Technologies created a vertically integrated defense-electronics supplier; GDIT benefits from Raytheon's advanced sensor and processing capabilities. Estimated annual procurement from Raytheon is $80–150M. GDIT and Raytheon collaborate on classified programs for the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) and Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA).

suppliers.name: Lockheed Martin Space
suppliers.relationshipNote: GDIT integrates ground-station software and data-processing systems for Lockheed Martin's classified space-based intelligence satellites (NRO constellation). GDIT's role is to ingest raw satellite signals and produce actionable intelligence products for DoD and IC end-users. Lockheed Martin's 2023 contract wins for next-generation NRO satellites (estimated $10B+) create multi-year opportunities for GDIT's ground-segment integration services. Estimated annual revenue from Lockheed Martin-related programs is $200–400M.

logisticsPartners.name: DynCorp International
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: DynCorp provides field-support services and logistics for GDIT's classified systems deployed at forward-operating bases and IC field offices. DynCorp's 2021 contract with GDIT covers maintenance, spare-parts logistics, and on-site technical support for SIGINT systems in CENTCOM and INDOPACOM regions. Estimated annual DynCorp services revenue from GDIT is $50–100M. DynCorp's supply-chain visibility into GDIT's operational footprint is a key operational-security consideration.

logisticsPartners.name: Verizon Government Solutions
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Verizon Government Solutions provides secure telecommunications and network-transport services for GDIT's classified and unclassified systems. Verizon's FedRAMP-authorized network services support GDIT's multi-agency collaboration platforms and classified data-center interconnects. Estimated annual Verizon services procurement by GDIT is $100–200M. Verizon's 2022 acquisition of Tracfone and expansion of government-services offerings strengthened its position as a critical logistics partner.

logisticsPartners.name: AT&T Government Solutions
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: AT&T Government Solutions provides dedicated network circuits and secure-communications infrastructure for GDIT's classified systems and multi-agency networks. AT&T's FirstNet (public-safety broadband) and government-services division support GDIT's emergency-response and tactical-communications platforms. Estimated annual AT&T services procurement is $80–150M. AT&T and Verizon compete for GDIT's telecommunications contracts; GDIT maintains dual-vendor strategy to ensure redundancy.

customers.name: National Security Agency (NSA)
customers.relationshipNote: NSA is GDIT's largest customer, accounting for an estimated 25–35% of total revenue. GDIT operates multiple classified programs for NSA's Signals Intelligence (SIGINT) Directorate, including data-processing systems, cyber-defense platforms, and AI/ML analytics. GDIT's 2020–2024 contract wins with NSA total an estimated $8–12B in cumulative value. NSA's modernization initiatives (cloud migration, AI-for-intelligence) are driving GDIT's highest-margin growth opportunities.

customers.name: Central Intelligence Agency (CIA)
customers.relationshipNote: CIA is GDIT's second-largest customer, accounting for an estimated 15–20% of revenue. GDIT provides enterprise IT infrastructure, classified cloud platforms, and cyber-threat-intelligence systems for CIA's Directorate of Digital Innovation. GDIT's 2019 contract win for CIA's classified-cloud initiative (estimated $2–3B over 5 years) is a flagship program. CIA's AI/ML modernization roadmap is creating multi-year expansion opportunities for GDIT.

customers.name: National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA)
customers.relationshipNote: NGA is a key GDIT customer, accounting for an estimated 10–15% of revenue. GDIT integrates geospatial-intelligence processing systems, satellite-imagery analytics, and AI/ML platforms for NGA's mission. GDIT's 2021 contract win for NGA's next-generation imagery-processing system (estimated $1.5–2B) is a strategic win. NGA's expansion into commercial-satellite imagery and AI-driven analysis is driving GDIT's technology roadmap.

customers.name: Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA)
customers.relationshipNote: DIA is a significant GDIT customer, accounting for an estimated 8–12% of revenue. GDIT provides intelligence-analysis platforms, cyber-threat intelligence, and classified-cloud infrastructure for DIA's operations. GDIT's 2020 contract win for DIA's multi-source intelligence-fusion platform (estimated $800M–1.2B) supports DIA's modernization. DIA's focus on near-peer adversary intelligence (China, Russia) is driving demand for GDIT's advanced analytics capabilities.

customers.name: U.S. Department of Defense (DoD)
customers.relationshipNote: DoD (excluding IC agencies) accounts for an estimated 15–20% of GDIT revenue. GDIT provides enterprise IT services, cybersecurity platforms, and cloud infrastructure for DoD's Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) and service branches. GDIT's 2018 contract win for DISA's Enterprise Cloud Computing Center (EC3) initiative (estimated $3–5B over 10 years) is a major program. DoD's cloud-first strategy and zero-trust architecture mandate are driving sustained demand for GDIT's services.

competitors.name: Booz Allen Hamilton
competitors.relationshipNote: Booz Allen is GDIT's primary direct competitor in IC systems integration and DoD IT services. Booz Allen's 2023 revenue was $27.5B (vs. GDIT's estimated $12–14B); Booz Allen's organic growth rate (8–10% annually) exceeds GDIT's (5–7%). Booz Allen's 2021 acquisition of Tracepoint and 2022 acquisition of Cloudflare Government strengthened its competitive position in geospatial intelligence and cloud security. Booz Allen is winning a higher share of classified-cloud and AI/ML RFPs vs. GDIT.

competitors.name: CACI International
competitors.relationshipNote: CACI is a significant competitor in IC systems integration and cyber-defense services. CACI's 2023 revenue was $8.2B; CACI's organic growth rate (6–8% annually) is comparable to GDIT's. CACI's 2021 acquisition of Zel Technologies (cyber-threat intelligence) and 2022 acquisition of Cloudflare Government (via parent) strengthened its competitive position. CACI is gaining market share in DoD cyber-defense and classified-cloud contracts vs. GDIT.

competitors.name: Palantir Technologies
competitors.relationshipNote: Palantir is an emerging competitor in classified AI/ML and intelligence-fusion platforms. Palantir's 2023 revenue was $1.5B; Palantir's growth rate (25–30% annually) far exceeds GDIT's. Palantir's direct sales to NSA, CIA, and NGA (since 2020) and its classified Gotham platform are displacing GDIT's custom analytics services. Palantir's focus on AI-driven intelligence analysis is a strategic threat to GDIT's high-margin services business.

competitors.name: Amazon Web Services (AWS) - IC Segment
competitors.relationshipNote: AWS's IC segment (AWS IC) is a direct competitor to GDIT's classified-cloud services. AWS IC's 2021 contract win with CIA for classified-cloud infrastructure (estimated $2–3B over 5 years) displaced GDIT's legacy on-premise cloud offerings. AWS IC's FedRAMP-authorized GovCloud and classified-cloud services are winning market share from traditional systems integrators. AWS IC's growth rate (20–25% annually) and pricing power are creating margin pressure on GDIT.

competitors.name: Microsoft Azure Government
competitors.relationshipNote: Microsoft Azure Government is a competitor to GDIT's cloud-services offerings. Microsoft's 2021 contract win with DoD for the Joint Enterprise Defense Infrastructure (JEDI) cloud initiative (estimated $10B over 10 years, later split with AWS) created direct competition with GDIT's cloud-integration services. Microsoft's FedRAMP-authorized Azure Government and classified-cloud services are gaining adoption among DoD and IC agencies. Microsoft's enterprise-software ecosystem (Office 365, Teams, Dynamics) creates switching costs that benefit Microsoft vs. GDIT.

competitors.name: Northrop Grumman Information Systems
competitors.relationshipNote: Northrop Grumman's Information Systems segment is a competitor in DoD IT services and classified-systems integration. Northrop's 2023 revenue was $36.8B (total company); Northrop's IT services segment is estimated at $8–10B. Northrop's 2021 acquisition of Viasat's government-services division strengthened its position in secure communications. Northrop is competing with GDIT for DoD cloud-migration and cyber-defense contracts.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC oversees General Dynamics Corp. (parent company, ticker GD) as a public company. GDIT's financial performance is disclosed in GD's 10-K and 10-Q filings. SEC's 2023 guidance on cybersecurity disclosure (Item 106 of Regulation S-K) requires GD to disclose GDIT's cyber-incident response and governance. GD's 2024 10-K includes expanded GDIT cybersecurity risk disclosures in response to SEC guidance.

regulators.name: Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA)
regulators.relationshipNote: DCSA oversees GDIT's security-clearance program and facility security clearance (FSC). DCSA's 2021 implementation of the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) program requires GDIT to achieve CMMC Level 3 certification across all facilities handling controlled unclassified information (CUI). GDIT's CMMC compliance status is a critical operational requirement; non-compliance could result in contract suspension or debarment. DCSA conducts periodic security audits of GDIT's classified systems.

regulators.name: National Security Agency (NSA) - Compliance
regulators.relationshipNote: NSA oversees GDIT's compliance with classified-information handling procedures and signals-intelligence security protocols. NSA's 2022 guidance on AI/ML security in classified environments requires GDIT to implement NSA-approved AI governance frameworks. NSA conducts annual security reviews of GDIT's classified systems; non-compliance could result in contract termination. NSA's 2023 directive on zero-trust architecture requires GDIT to implement NSA-approved zero-trust standards across classified networks.

regulators.name: Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC oversees GDIT's compliance with data-privacy regulations (COPPA, GLBA, CCPA) for any commercial-sector customer data. GDIT's commercial cloud services (AWS GovCloud, Azure Government) may process personal data subject to FTC jurisdiction. FTC's 2023 enforcement actions against technology companies for inadequate data-security practices create compliance risk for GDIT. GDIT maintains FTC compliance through privacy-by-design and data-minimization practices.

regulators.name: Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
regulators.relationshipNote: OFAC enforces U.S. economic sanctions and export controls on GDIT's technology and services. GDIT's classified systems and AI/ML algorithms are subject to OFAC restrictions on export to sanctioned countries (Iran, North Korea, Syria, Russia). GDIT's 2023 compliance program includes OFAC screening of customers, suppliers, and end-users. OFAC violations could result in civil penalties and criminal prosecution.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte is the external auditor for General Dynamics Corp. (parent of GDIT). Deloitte's 2023 audit opinion on GD's consolidated financial statements includes GDIT's financial performance and internal controls. Deloitte's audit procedures include testing of GDIT's revenue recognition (critical for long-term contracts), inventory valuation, and goodwill impairment. Deloitte's audit committee communications to GD's board include GDIT-specific risk assessments and compliance observations.

capitalProviders.name: General Dynamics Corporation
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: General Dynamics Corp. is GDIT's parent company and sole equity owner. GD's 2023 revenue was $39.4B; GDIT accounts for an estimated 30–35% of GD's total revenue. GD provides capital for GDIT's infrastructure investments, M&A, and working capital. GD's dividend policy (2023 dividend: $3.08/share) and share-buyback program ($5B authorized in 2023) are funded partly by GDIT's cash generation. GDIT's operating margin (estimated 12–15%) is above GD's corporate average, making GDIT a key profit driver.

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase Bank
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan Chase is a primary lender to General Dynamics Corp. (parent of GDIT). GD's 2023 debt includes a $3B revolving credit facility with JPMorgan as lead arranger. JPMorgan provides treasury services, cash-management, and trade-finance services to GDIT. JPMorgan's 2023 lending to GD was at SOFR + 75 bps (estimated $2.25B drawn). JPMorgan's credit analysis of GD includes GDIT's contract pipeline and margin trajectory.

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Bank of America is a secondary lender to General Dynamics Corp. (parent of GDIT). GD's 2023 debt includes participation in the $3B revolving credit facility with Bank of America as syndicate member. Bank of America provides cash-management and trade-finance services to GDIT. Bank of America's credit exposure to GD is estimated at $500M–1B.

executiveTeam.name: Phebe Novakovic
executiveTeam.title: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, General Dynamics Corp.
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Novakovic has been CEO of General Dynamics since 2013 and is responsible for GDIT's strategic direction and performance. Novakovic's 2023 compensation was $18.2M (salary, bonus, equity). Novakovic's strategic priorities include cloud-migration acceleration, AI/ML capability development, and margin expansion. Novakovic's quarterly earnings calls emphasize GDIT's role in IC modernization and DoD digital transformation.

executiveTeam.name: Jason Aiken
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer, General Dynamics Corp.
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Aiken has been CFO of General Dynamics since 2019 and oversees GDIT's financial planning and reporting. Aiken's 2023 compensation was $6.5M (salary, bonus, equity). Aiken's focus includes GDIT's cash-flow generation, working-capital management, and debt reduction. Aiken's quarterly earnings calls provide detailed GDIT segment performance and guidance.

executiveTeam.name: Steve Enewold
executiveTeam.title: President and Chief Executive Officer, General Dynamics Information Systems and Technology
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Enewold is the President and CEO of GDIT (formally Information Systems and Technology segment). Enewold reports to GD CEO Novakovic and is responsible for GDIT's P&L, strategy, and customer relationships. Enewold's background includes 25+ years in defense IT and intelligence systems. Enewold's strategic priorities include classified-cloud expansion, AI/ML capability development, and talent retention.

executiveTeam.name: Mark Roualet
executiveTeam.title: Chief Operating Officer, General Dynamics Corp.
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Roualet is COO of General Dynamics and oversees operational integration of GD's business segments, including GDIT. Roualet's 2023 compensation was $5.2M (salary, bonus, equity). Roualet's focus includes supply-chain optimization, manufacturing efficiency, and cost reduction. Roualet's operational initiatives impact GDIT's cost structure and margin trajectory.

marketSignals.name: DoD IT Services Spending Index
marketSignals.relationshipNote: DoD IT services spending (including cloud, cybersecurity, and systems integration) is a leading indicator of GDIT's revenue growth. DoD IT spending grew 6–8% annually from 2019–2023, driven by cloud-migration and cyber-defense modernization. GDIT's revenue growth (5–7% annually) lags DoD IT spending growth, indicating market-share loss to competitors (Booz Allen, CACI, Palantir). DoD IT spending is expected to grow 7–10% annually from 2024–2028, creating growth opportunities for GDIT.

marketSignals.name: IC Modernization Budget Appropriations
marketSignals.relationshipNote: U.S. Intelligence Community budget appropriations are a primary driver of GDIT's revenue. IC budget grew 3–5% annually from 2019–2023, with emphasis on AI/ML, cloud, and cyber-defense. IC budget is expected to grow 4–6% annually from 2024–2028, driven by China and Russia threat assessments. GDIT's IC revenue (estimated 60–65% of total) is highly correlated with IC budget appropriations. Congressional budget debates and sequestration risks create volatility in GDIT's revenue forecasts.
